> [!IMPORTANT] > Get OpenCode Mod only from [Subhashis360/opencode-mod](https://github.com/Subhashis360/opencode-mod). > It is an unofficial community extension, not made by the OpenCode team. The old standalone > "OpenCode Mod" desktop app is discontinued: uninstall it and use this extension inside the official OpenCode app.



--- Want OpenCode to do more than edit code? Add this extension and its agent can open and control your desktop apps and Android phone. It can also use any OpenAI-compatible provider, with the model list fetched for you, and run prompts on a schedule while you're away. OpenCode Mod is a plugin for the official **OpenCode Desktop** app. It adds a **Settings → Mod** page with twelve tabs, so agents, providers, MCP servers, permissions, hooks and memory are set up with forms instead of hand-edited JSON. Everything is saved in your normal OpenCode config, keeps working without the extension, and runs locally on your computer. ## Quick start You need [OpenCode Desktop](https://opencode.ai) **2.2 or newer** and [Git](https://git-scm.com). Computer use needs Windows; everything else works on Windows, macOS and Linux. The built files ship in the repository, so there is nothing to compile. ### Ask your agent Paste this into any coding agent that can run commands on your computer: OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and others. ```text Install the OpenCode Mod extension for OpenCode Desktop from https://github.com/Subhashis360/opencode-mod 1. Check that git is installed. Clone the repository into a permanent folder in my home directory (for example ~/opencode-mod). If that folder already exists and is this repository, run `git pull` in it instead. 2. Open my global OpenCode config: ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json (on Windows: C:\Users\\.config\opencode\opencode.json). Create the file with {} if it does not exist. 3. Add the absolute path of the cloned folder, written with forward slashes, to the "plugins" array (create the array if it is missing). Keep every other setting and every existing plugin exactly as it is, keep the file valid JSON/JSONC, and do not add the path twice. 4. Do not change anything else. Do not run npm install: the built files are already in the repository. 5. Show me the "plugins" line you wrote, then tell me to restart OpenCode Desktop (2.2 or newer) and open Settings → Mod, or press Ctrl+Shift+P and type "Mod". ``` ### Install by hand ```bash git clone https://github.com/Subhashis360/opencode-mod.git ``` Add the cloned folder to `plugins` in your **global** OpenCode config, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (on Windows `C:\Users\\.config\opencode\opencode.json`): ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": ["C:/Users//opencode-mod"] } ``` Use forward slashes on Windows too, and keep any plugins you already have. Restart OpenCode Desktop and open **Settings → Mod**, or press `Ctrl+Shift+P` and type **Mod**. ### Update and uninstall The extension updates itself: each time OpenCode starts it checks this repository and installs an update in the background, then asks for a restart. Turn that off, or check and update with one click, in Mod → Updates. `git pull` in the folder still works. To uninstall, remove the line from `plugins` and restart OpenCode. Your settings stay in your config and do nothing on their own. ## How it works OpenCode Desktop 2.2 loads plugins listed in the global `opencode.json`. OpenCode Mod has two parts: | Part | Runs in | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | Server part (`dist/server.js`) | OpenCode's local server | Adds the `computer`, `schedule` and `memory` tools, the hooks, the screenshot clean-up, and the API the settings page calls | | Desktop part (`dist/gui-experimental.cjs`) | OpenCode Desktop's windows and main process | Adds the **Settings → Mod** page and commands, the tray icon, and the runner that starts scheduled tasks | You talk to your agent as usual. When it needs your desktop it calls the `computer` tool, asks you before touching each app, and works through Windows UI Automation and OCR before falling back to screenshots. Settings you change in **Mod** are written to your OpenCode config, so OpenCode and the agent pick them up on the next message. ## What the OpenCode extension adds | Group | Tab | What you get | | --- | --- | --- | | **Agent** | Agents | Custom agents with their own prompt, model, color and tool limits, from templates such as **Security Auditor** and **Bug Bounty Assistant** | | | System prompt | The exact prompt OpenCode gives each model, editable per agent, plus your own prompt library | | | Commands | Custom slash commands with a prompt, agent and model (`/review`, `/audit`, `/tests`, `/fix` templates) | | | Memory | Facts the agent saves about you and each project, added to every new session | | **Tools** | MCP servers | Local or remote MCP servers with a form (Playwright, Context7, GitHub, Filesystem templates) | | | Computer use | The agent sees and controls Windows apps and Android phones, with per-app approval | | | Hooks | Your shell commands before or after tool calls, on prompts, on idle and on errors | | | Permissions | Presets (Read-only audit, Safe, Balanced, Full auto) and per-tool allow / ask / deny | | **Models** | Providers | **Edit custom providers and fetch their models** from the provider's API | | | Session limits | Your free-model usage today and over the last week | | **Automation and speed** | Scheduled | Prompts that run once, every N minutes, daily, weekly, monthly or on a cron, with notifications | | | Experimental | **Parallel web search**, warm sessions, background compaction and other speed settings | ## Highlights ### Edit any provider and fetch its models OpenCode's own Providers page can only rename or remove a provider. **Mod → Providers** (or **Edit custom providers** in the command palette) edits the base URL, API key, headers and AI SDK package of any OpenAI-compatible provider, and **fetches its model list** so you only tick the models you want. It has templates for OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, NVIDIA NIM and Together. Fetching uses the key you typed or the one you already connected in OpenCode, and runs through OpenCode's local server, so the provider's CORS rules don't block it. ### Computer use in OpenCode The agent opens apps, reads windows, clicks, types and checks its own work, on Windows and on Android phones over `adb`. It reads windows as numbered text first, which is faster and works with text-only models. With **Don't use my cursor** on, it presses buttons through accessibility while you keep using your mouse. A glow outlines the app it is using and disappears when the run ends. Screenshot files are deleted as soon as they are read, and older screenshots are dropped from the conversation so every step stays quick. ### Pentest and bug bounty agents in two clicks **Security Auditor** reviews code for vulnerabilities without changing it and reports each finding with severity, location and fix. **Bug Bounty Assistant** is for authorized pentests, bug bounty programs and CTFs: it plans recon and test cases, builds minimal proofs of concept and writes findings in report format, asking before it runs commands. Code Reviewer, Debugger, Test Writer, Architect and Docs Writer cover everyday work. ### A faster agent: Parallel web search and warm sessions **Mod → Experimental → Speed** brings together the settings that make OpenCode respond faster. You can switch web search to [Parallel](https://parallel.ai), Exa or Tavily, or rotate between them when one is rate limited. You can also keep recent sessions' prompt caches warm, summarize long chats in the background, turn off undo snapshots in big projects, store media compactly, and cap tool output. ## FAQ
Is this an OpenCode extension or a separate app? An extension. It is a plugin package that OpenCode Desktop 2.2+ loads from your config, with a server part and a desktop part. The old standalone OpenCode Mod app is discontinued.
How do I install a plugin in OpenCode Desktop? Add the plugin's folder or package to `plugins` in your global `opencode.json` and restart the app. See [Quick start](#quick-start) and OpenCode's [GUI plugin docs](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/gui).
Does OpenCode support computer use? Not by itself. This extension adds a `computer` tool for Windows apps and Android phones, with approval for each app.
How do I edit a custom provider or fetch its models in OpenCode? Open **Settings → Mod → Providers**, press **Edit** on the provider, then **Fetch models**.
Does it work with OpenCode's free models and my own API keys? Yes. It runs inside the official app, so your sign-in, OpenCode's free models and your own keys all work as usual.
Does it send my data anywhere? No. The extension runs locally. Your agent's messages go to the model provider you chose, as they always do in OpenCode. Hooks only come from your global config folder, never from a project, so a cloned repository can't plant commands.
What should I do if something breaks? Run `git pull` in the extension folder and restart OpenCode. If the problem stays, [open an issue](https://github.com/Subhashis360/opencode-mod/issues) with your OpenCode version, what you did and what you saw.
## Build from source ```bash npm install --legacy-peer-deps npm run build ``` `dist/server.js` is the server part and `dist/gui-experimental.cjs` the desktop part. Set `ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1` before `npm install` to skip Electron's download; only its types are used. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Show me the "plugins" line you wrote, then tell me to restart OpenCode Desktop (2.2 or newer) and open Settings → Mod, or press Ctrl+Shift+P and type "Mod". ``` ### ख़ुद इंस्टॉल करें रिपॉज़िटरी क्लोन करें, फिर फ़ोल्डर का पाथ ग्लोबल कॉन्फ़िग `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` में `plugins` में जोड़ें (Windows पर भी फ़ॉरवर्ड स्लैश): ```jsonc { "plugins": ["C:/Users//opencode-mod"] } ``` OpenCode Desktop दोबारा शुरू करें और **Settings → Mod** खोलें, या `Ctrl+Shift+P` दबाकर **Mod** लिखें। ## फ़ीचर - **कस्टम प्रोवाइडर एडिट करें और मॉडल लाएँ**: Base URL, API key, हेडर बदलें और प्रोवाइडर की API से मॉडल सूची लाकर चुनें (OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, NVIDIA NIM आदि)। - **कंप्यूटर यूज़**: एजेंट Windows ऐप और Android फ़ोन चला सकता है; हर ऐप के लिए पहली बार आपकी मंज़ूरी चाहिए, स्क्रीनशॉट पढ़ते ही डिलीट हो जाते हैं। - **तैयार एजेंट टेम्पलेट**: Security Auditor, Bug Bounty Assistant (पेनटेस्टिंग और बग बाउंटी के लिए), Code Reviewer, Debugger वगैरह। - **स्पीड सेटिंग्स**: Parallel वेब सर्च (Exa, Tavily भी), सेशन को warm रखना, बैकग्राउंड कॉम्पैक्शन वगैरह। - **ऑटोमेशन**: शेड्यूल्ड टास्क, हुक्स, ऑटो मेमोरी, MCP सर्वर, परमिशन प्रीसेट, सिस्टम प्रॉम्प्ट एडिटिंग। पूरी जानकारी, स्क्रीनशॉट और FAQ के लिए [English README](../../README.md) देखें।

Save when you learn something durable and useful later:
- the user's preferences and working style ("prefers pnpm", "wants short answers", "never push without asking")
- project conventions, decisions and their reasons, commands that work, gotchas you hit
- corrections the user gives you, so the same mistake does not happen again

Do not save: things already in the code, git history or AGENTS.md; one-off task details; secrets, tokens or passwords; guesses.

Actions: save (text, scope), update (id, text), forget (id), list.
scope "global" = about the user, everywhere. scope "project" (default) = only this project.
Keep each fact to one short sentence. Before saving, check the <memory> block and update an existing entry instead of adding a near-duplicate. Forget entries that turn out to be wrong.

Searches this project's code index: a local index of every source file, its declarations (functions, classes, methods, types), its imports and its code chunks, kept current as files change. Use it before grep or glob to find where something is: it answers in one call with file:line references you can open with the read tool, instead of many searches and reads.

Actions:
- search: find code by what it does or by a name. query is plain language ("where are auth tokens refreshed", "retry with backoff") or an identifier. Returns the best matching code chunks with line numbers. Set full=true to see whole chunks.
- symbols: find declarations by name, exact or partial (query "UserServ" finds UserService). Optional kind: function, method, class, interface, type, enum, struct, trait, module, variable, macro.
- references: everything that uses one identifier (symbol): its definitions, calls, imports and other uses, each with the function or class it sits in. Use it for "who calls X" and before renaming or changing a signature.
- outline: the declarations of one file (file), as a tree with line ranges. Cheaper than reading the whole file.
- dependencies: what one file (file) imports and which project files import it.
- status: how many files the index holds and whether it is updating.

path narrows search, symbols and references to files whose path contains it (e.g. "src/server"). Paths are relative to the project folder. The index matches words and names, not exact text: use grep for an exact string or a regular expression.

Controls the user's desktop, and Android phones over adb: sees the screen, clicks and taps, types, presses keys, scrolls, opens apps and uses the clipboard. Use it for native apps, phones and anything outside the project files.

Before driving any screen, pick the fastest way to the result. Think about where the data or action really lives:
1. Files, settings, command-line tools, APIs and feeds: the shell and webfetch tools do it in one step, with no screen at all (for example a game's or service's public API, an app's export, a log file, `winget`, `Get-Process`).
2. Public web pages: webfetch reads them as text. Pages that need the user's login or clicks run in their browser window, and Chrome, Edge and Firefox expose page content to accessibility, so read_window, click_element and set_value work on them too.
3. Desktop apps: read_window, click_element, set_value, wait_for and watch work through accessibility as text, with no picture.
4. Screenshots and pointer clicks: only for what has no text (canvases, images, games drawn as pictures) or when the faster ways fail.
To follow something over time (new messages, a download, a build, a game's moves) use watch or wait_for, never repeated screenshots.

Every look comes with a screen map. Act on it, not on pixels you estimate from the picture:
- A screenshot comes with a text map of the whole display: each window, the named groups inside it, and every control and piece of visible text as a line like `[12] button "Login" @412,88 disabled` or `[30] ocr "Start Game" @150,250`. The same [n] is drawn on the picture next to the element, so the picture and the text point at the same things. `ocr` lines are text an app draws itself (games, canvases, web pages), read by Windows OCR.
- Pass ref: n to act on an element: click_element, set_value, left_click, double_click, right_click, mouse_move, scroll, zoom, type (clicks the field first), left_click_drag (start_ref and ref). The tool looks the element up again where it is now, so a ref never clicks where something used to be, and it fails clearly when the element is gone or covered. Refs stay the same while an element stays on screen, so you can plan several steps from one look.
- A ref only ever means the element it was given to. If that element is removed and another with the same name takes its place (the next row's "Delete" after a row is deleted), the action fails with STALE_REF instead of pressing the newcomer.
- Several elements can share a name (three "Login" buttons). The map shows which group each sits in; pick by ref. Text lookups that match several elements equally fail and list them with refs instead of guessing. 'Admin > Login' means the Login inside the group or window "Admin".
- Each coordinate click reports what it landed on (`-> button "Login" in "Sign in"`). If that is not what you meant, fix it before going on.

Work quickly. Every model turn costs several seconds, far more than any action, so the fastest run has the fewest calls:
- read_window lists the controls of the app you are working in (the last app you clicked, typed into, switched to or opened) as text, without a picture, even when OpenCode is in front of it. Pass text to filter it, or coordinate to read the window under that point.
- click_element (ref or text) presses buttons, checkboxes, tabs, menu and list items through accessibility in the background: the user's mouse does not move and the app may stay behind other windows. OCR text and controls without an accessible action get a real click.
- set_value (ref or text, value) fills a field, picks a drop-down or list option, sets a checkbox (true/false) or a slider (number) in one step, instead of click + select-all + type. It reads the result back.
- wait_for (text, duration = timeout seconds, gone?) waits until text appears (or with gone: true, disappears) in a window title, the app or on screen, checking several times a second. Use it instead of wait + screenshot for dialogs, loading and saving.
- watch (text?, duration = timeout seconds, default 10, max 120) waits until new text appears in the app you are working in (new chat messages, notifications, log lines) and returns only the new lines, with no picture. The first watch of a window notes what is already there. text keeps only lines containing it.
- Busy apps (chat apps, IDE-like tools, big tables): read_window with skeleton: true first lists the window's named groups as a tree with ids and element counts; then read_window with within: "g12" lists just that group, with the whole element limit spent on it.
- inspect (ref or text) shows everything about one control: its value or full text, range, scroll position, selection, children and the actions it supports. expand, collapse, select, focus and scroll_to (ref or text) do those directly through accessibility; scroll_to and inspect also reach a control scrolled out of view by its exact name.
- switch_window (text) brings an open app or window to the front. list_windows lists every app window with its state and where it is. minimize_window, maximize_window, restore_window and close_window act on the window named in text (default: the app you are working in); move_window takes region [x0, y0, x1, y1] for new bounds or coordinate for a new top-left corner. close_window asks the app to close the way its close button does, so it may ask to save first.
- Plan the task and send it as one call with actions: [...] (run in order, stopping at the first failure, which is reported). E.g. [click_element ref 12, wait_for "Save As", set_value "File name" = "report.pdf", click_element "Save", wait_for "Save As" gone: true]. One call with five steps is five times faster than five calls.
- Clicks, drag, scroll, key, type, wait, open_application and switch_window return a fresh screenshot and map automatically, taken once the screen stops changing. Never follow them with a separate screenshot call; set screenshot_after: false only when you will not need to look before your next call. Use marks: false for a clean picture when the numbers would hide what you need to see (a game board), and zoom (region or ref) for small details.
- Do not add a wait between steps. Every click, key, type, scroll, drag and open already waits for the screen to settle before it hands back its screenshot, so what you get is already current — a wait on top of that just burns a whole model turn (several seconds) and the pause itself, and makes the run feel slow. When something loads, saves, downloads or appears on its own, use wait_for or watch: they return the instant it is ready instead of pausing a fixed guess. Reach for plain wait only in the rare case where nothing on screen ever signals that the app is ready (a splash with no text, a timed animation), and keep the duration as short as will do.

Coordinates:
- All coordinates are in the screenshot frame of the current display (shown by screenshot, read_window and list_displays), not physical pixels. Display 0 is the primary; pass display to switch.

Errors start with a code and say whether trying again can help, for example `STALE_REF (look again before retrying): ...`:
- safe to retry: nothing happened that repeating could double (a read that timed out). Repeat it as is.
- look again before retrying: the screen changed under the action (STALE_REF, NOT_FOUND, DISABLED). Look, then act on the new refs.
- do not retry: the same call will fail again (AMBIGUOUS_TARGET: pass a ref; COVERED: switch_window or click_element; BLOCKED, UNSUPPORTED, INVALID_ARGS: change the approach).

Actions:
- screenshot (marks?), zoom (region or ref), read_window (text?, coordinate?, skeleton?, within?), inspect (ref or text), list_displays, list_windows, cursor_position
- click_element (ref or text), set_value (ref or text, value; '' clears a field), expand, collapse, select, focus, scroll_to (ref or text), wait_for (text, duration?, gone?), watch (text?, duration?)
- switch_window (text), minimize_window, maximize_window, restore_window, close_window (text?), move_window (text?, region or coordinate)
- mouse_move, left_click, right_click, middle_click, double_click, triple_click (ref or coordinate; omit both to use the cursor position; text holds modifier keys such as "shift" or "ctrl")
- left_click_drag (start_ref or start_coordinate, ref or coordinate), left_mouse_down, left_mouse_up
- scroll (ref or coordinate?, scroll_direction, scroll_amount)
- type (text, ref?), key (text: "ctrl+s", "alt+tab", "Return", or space-separated sequences like "Down Down Enter"), hold_key (text, duration)
- wait (duration in seconds, max 10): a last-resort fixed pause — avoid it, prefer wait_for or watch, and never add it just to let the screen update after an action

- Phone screens change under every tap, so a ref is tapped where it was in the last look. Take the screenshot that comes back after each action before tapping refs from an older look.

- The user approves each app (and each phone) the first time it is controlled. If they deny, stop and ask them what to do.

- OpenCode's own window cannot be controlled.
- When the user turns on "Don't use my cursor" in Settings, nothing moves their mouse: left_click with ref presses the element through accessibility, type with ref focuses the field without a click, and other pointer actions (coordinate clicks, right/double clicks, drag, scroll, mouse_move) are refused.
